fields.v: Ouyang, Y., Huang, X., Liu, B., Zheng, Z., Gu, Y., Zhang, X. (2026). Benchmarks are Not Enough: Ramp for Runtime Assessing of Agentic Models in Production Systems. arXiv:2605.27492v1 [cs.SE], 26 May 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2605.27492v1 [cs.SE]; no venue stated (timeline footnote: draft completed 14 May 2026)
School of Computer Science and Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China (all authors); authors' lab runs the YatCC platform and the AI Hub gateway

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — RAMP, a production-grounded assessment infrastructure on the YatCC platform with six serially dependent compiler-construction tasks (T0-T5), a resurrection protocol (golden-artifact injection after failure), outcome/process metrics and a composite Agent Efficiency Index (AEI); 15 models compared on one OpenHands-SDK backend

No SDD approach. Agent: unified backend built on the OpenHands SDK (version not stated), models accessed through the authors' AI Hub OpenAI-compatible gateway. Models (Table 3): claude-opus-4-7, gpt-5.5, deepseek-v4-pro, qwen3.6-max-preview, glm-5.1, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-reasoner, qwen3.5-plus, glm-4.7, kimi-k2.5, glm-4.6, deepseek-chat, qwen3-coder-flash, minimax-m2.5. Baseline: unmodified scaffold code without agent

Task artefacts: partially implemented YatCC scaffold repository per task; intermediate artifacts passed between stages (token stream, AST/ASG JSON, LLVM IR, optimized IR, RV64 assembly); golden artifacts from a reference implementation; config.cmake switches (TASK_k_REVIVE=ON) for resurrection

Evaluation flow: fresh container and workspace (LLVM 14, ANTLR, pybind11, CMake) -> agent executes T0 env setup, T1 lexer, T2 parser, T3 IR generation, T4 IR optimization, T5 RV64 assembly sequentially in one persistent repository -> per-task deterministic test suites (0-100) -> Mode 1: resurrection (golden artifact injected when score < threshold, e.g. 60%, agent not informed) or Mode 2: no resurrection (cascading failures); max 500 dialogue turns across the pipeline

Quality verdict against the authors' end-to-end criterion (a tier is reached only if every task up to it is correctly and completely accomplished; completion = score 100): does not work for all 15 agent configurations (none completes T0-T5) and does not work for the baseline. Note: the authors also name a per-task passing threshold of 60 (bold in Table 4, resurrection trigger); under that threshold Opus-4.7 passes all six tasks. Cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations; N/A for the baseline)
fields.why: Baseline row had metric values but no verdict (every configuration, baseline included, gets its own verdict). Two criteria are stated: the end-to-end 'correctly and completely accomplishes every task' rule (Opus-4.7 fails, T4 68.4) and a per-task pass threshold of 60 (Opus-4.7 passes every task), so Opus-4.7 could be 'does not work' or 'partly'.
fields.doubt: Há dois critérios: tarefa completa (100) e limiar de 60% por tarefa. Pelo limiar de 60, o Opus-4.7 passa todas as tarefas. Decide qual critério usar e se o Opus-4.7 fica 'does not work' ou 'partly'.

fields.v: Tasks: YatCC T0-T5 serial pipeline. Configurations: 15 models on the same OpenHands-SDK backend, AI Hub gateway, environment, toolchain, prompts and orchestration policies; non-agent baseline (unmodified scaffold). Held constant: agent backend, prompts, hardware (AMD EPYC 7742, 256 GB, Debian 11), 500-turn cap. Acceptance: dedicated deterministic test suites per task. Repetitions: one run per model (authors: 15 model tests, not sufficient for statistical conclusions). Human intervention: none. Model settings (temperature, reasoning effort) not stated

Opus-4.7 highest MR (93.39) but highest cost ($126.24, 14.5x DS-v4-Pro for a 9.4% MR gain); DS-v4-Pro second (85.34, $8.68); GPT-5.5 highest AEI (81.57, MR 65.91). Cost range $0.05-$126.24 (2,525x). Stage completion rates 100% (T0), 46.7% (T1), 26.7% (T2), 13.3% (T3), 0% (T4), 20% (T5); average MR 42.7, reported as 17.6 points above the non-agent baseline. Context failure most frequent hard-stop cause (9 of 15), planning failure 2, reasoning failure 1; planning failure observed in 8 of 15. OLS: cost explains about 52% and time about 40% of MR variance. No significance tests

Per the authors, yes: serial pipeline exposes capability decline, failure propagation and cost differences invisible to isolated benchmarks; AEI re-ranks models relative to MR. Repeatability not assessed (single run per model). Resurrection mode (Mode 1) claimed to improve diagnostic observability, but no Mode 1 results are reported. Limitations stated: one domain, 15 runs, single agent backend, possible contamination (YatCC public), subjective equal AEI weights

Compiler construction only, may not represent other production domains; 15 model tests insufficient for fine-grained statistical conclusions across model families, scaffolds or repeated runs; all runs on OpenHands backend; YatCC public, contamination risk; AEI equal weighting subjective. Future work: more models and agent frameworks, repeated runs under controlled settings to separate model, scaffold and orchestration effects; improved AEI (scenario weights, Pareto analysis, recovery metrics); harder variants with reduced or removed scaffolding

Values from Table 4 (p. 8) and text p. 9-13. Inconsistencies: text says 8 models score 100 on T1, Table 4 shows 7 (consistent with the 46.7% completion rate); average MR stated as 42.7, Table 4 values average about 43.2, and 42.7 minus baseline 23.38 is 19.3, not the stated 17.6; text says only 'proprietary models like DS-v4-Pro and Qwen-3.6-Max reach T3 with none progressing further', but Table 4 also gives Opus-4.7 and GPT-5.5 100 on T3 and Opus-4.7 100 on T5; Mode 1 (resurrection) is called the default producing the primary leaderboard, but all reported runs use Mode 2, while MR is defined with a resurrection factor; Figure 6 caption repeats the radar-chart caption of Figure 7. GLM-4.6 cost not reported. Repository and leaderboard said to be open-sourced (ramp.yatcc-ai.com; YatCC on GitHub, arcsysu/YatCC). Footnote: results of extra backends to be added. No pre-registration. Programming language: implementation language not stated (toolchain LLVM 14, ANTLR, pybind11, CMake); the compiler input is C source code

fields.why: The compared objects (15 models, OpenHands SDK) are third-party, but the authors built RAMP, YatCC, the AI Hub gateway and the unified agent backend on top of the OpenHands SDK (footnote 2), and state 'We evaluate RAMP'. Whether their own evaluation infrastructure counts as an evaluated tool (Partly) or not (Yes) is a judgement.
fields.doubt: Os modelos e o OpenHands SDK são de terceiros, mas o backend do agente, o RAMP e o YatCC são dos autores, que dizem 'We evaluate RAMP'. Decide se Q12 fica Yes ou Partly.
